stratcomments:
Was Floian-Dapingian.

Ebbestad & Lefebre: "The detailed, revised biostratigraphic framework produced by Martin et al. (in press) based on both graptolites and acritarchs confirms the late Tremadocian age (A. murrayi biozone) for low-diversity assemblages occurring in the lower part of the succession (between 240 and 300 m above the contact with underlying Cambrian strata). It also confirms that high-diversity faunas are found predominantly in the upper part of the Fezouata Shale, either in latest Tremadocian (H. copiosus biozone: Z-F0) or in early Floian deposits (Z-F24 and Z-F26). However, extensive field work in the Lower Ordovician of Zagora area (2012-2014, ANR project RALI) clearly suggests a late Tremadocian age (A. murrayi Biozone) for the Z-F5 assemblage. The Z-F5 fauna is thus older than all other high-diversity Early Ordovician."

COMMENTS: Collection name listed as "S2/f522" in Cooper (1979) but as this is out of sequence (ascending numbers), the enterer regards the collection to truely be "S2/f552".

stratcomments: "A closer examination of theis locality, which is located in the northwest corner between teh road and the stream, showed that trinucleus slate is not to be found here. The slate is loose, grey, very poor in fossils and thus certainly resembles petrographically the loose, gray trinucleus slate, such as it generally occurs in this area, but on careful examination, among other fossils, the river Monograptus personatus was found here, where the layers must belong to the cyrtograptus slate."
geogcomments: Based on location of Jarrestad, Sweden
